title: Corporate Governance and Regulatory Compliance

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk
children.blurb: Board advisory and fiduciary risk covers the duties directors owe when artificial intelligence enters the decisions, products or operations of a company.

children.name: Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing
children.blurb: Supply chain and sustainability auditing covers the review of a company's suppliers, subcontractors and material flows against environmental, labour and reporting obligations.

children.name: Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection
children.blurb: Insider trading and market abuse detection covers the use of artificial intelligence to find suspicious trading patterns, communications and relationships that may indicate misuse of material non public information or other market misconduct.

children.name: Regulatory Change Mapping
children.blurb: Regulatory change mapping is the practice of tracking new statutes, rules, guidance and court decisions that affect how an organisation may use artificial intelligence, then connecting each change to the internal policies, contracts and controls it touches.

children.name: Merger and Restructuring Analysis
children.blurb: Merger and restructuring analysis covers the work of assessing whether a proposed combination, divestiture or reorganisation makes sense and can be completed.

sections.body: Corporate governance and regulatory compliance is the work of keeping a company's decisions, disclosures and trading inside the rules that apply to it, and artificial intelligence is now used across that work rather than only discussed as a future possibility. Systems read board papers and minutes to surface conflicts of interest, related party dealings and gaps in oversight, and they scan supplier records and sustainability disclosures against audit criteria. Surveillance models watch order book and communications data for patterns that resemble insider dealing or market abuse, while text pipelines track regulatory publications and map each change onto the policies and controls it touches. In mergers and restructuring, models test combinations of entities, assets and liabilities against competition and disclosure rules before advisers commit to a structure. The common thread is scale: these are tasks defined by large document sets, cross references and pattern detection, which is where machine learning performs reliably and where human review alone becomes slow and uneven.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The strongest results are in retrieval and classification. Finding the clause that changed, matching a supplier certificate to a standard, or flagging an unusual trade sequence are now routine enough that many compliance teams treat them as baseline tooling. What remains unsolved is judgement under ambiguity: whether a particular conflict is material, whether a disclosure satisfies a principles based rule, or whether a restructuring will be challenged, still turns on facts and precedent that models handle unevenly. Detection systems also produce false positives at rates that make alert triage a real cost, and their outputs are only as good as the data feeding them, which in governance settings is often incomplete or inconsistently labelled. Explainability matters here because a regulator or a court may ask why a flag was raised, and a model that cannot answer that question is of limited use. Nothing in this work removes the fiduciary duties of directors or the accountability of advisers, and the honest limit is that these tools support review rather than replaceit.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here divide the field by the decision being supported. Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk covers the oversight layer, where conflicts, related party transactions and the quality of board information are examined, and a reader goes there for the duties that sit with directors. Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing deals with the evidence trail behind environmental and labour claims, useful when the question is what a company can actually verify about its suppliers. Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection is the market facing page, concerned with trading patterns and communications, and it is the place to look for surveillance and alerting. Regulatory Change Mapping addresses the inflow of new rules and how they are traced to internal policies, which matters when the problem is keeping pace rather than investigating a single event. Merger and Restructuring Analysis brings these threads together around transactions, where competition, disclosure and governance questions converge, and it is the natural entry point for deal specific work. Read together, they move from the boardroom outward to suppliers, markets and regulators, then back to the transaction that tests all of them.
